adarel-sa.history: Adarel SA appears in the INAVI winery registry with a facility at Ruta 6 km 29.800, Sauce, Canelones. It shares its address, telephone and contact email with Avisara SA, another company registered with INAVI. No website, commercial brand or published information about its wines was found.
highlights: Shares its INAVI address and contact details with Avisara SA (Ruta 6 km 29.800, Sauce)

alejandro-de-maio.history: Bodegas De Maio, owned by the De Maio family, is located near Pando (Canelones). It began more than twenty years ago with a table wine and today hosts tastings in Pando; in 2024 it supplied grapes to a project by winemaker Martín Viggiano.

alto-de-la-ballena.history: Founded in 1998 by the married couple Paula Pivel and Álvaro Lorenzo. In 2000 they bought almost 20 hectares in the Sierra de la Ballena, planted in the spring of 2001, made their first harvest in 2005 and released their first wines in 2007.
highlights: Vineyard on the slopes of the Sierra de la Ballena, about 15 km from the coast.
In the upper sections, thin soil over decomposed Precambrian granite and schist.
Syrah on the highest, stoniest ground; Tannat and Merlot at the foot of the slope.
alto-de-la-ballena.flagship_grapes: Tannat with a small percentage of Viognier

angel-fallabrino-sa.history: Family winery in Melilla, in the rural northwest of Montevideo, presented as a historic site and run by Italian descendants of the Fallabrino family. It welcomes visitors with winery tours, tastings and Uruguayan asado (barbecue) workshops sold through tour operators.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with tours, a shop and a restaurant.
Offers Uruguayan asado experiences and winery visits via Civitatis and Airbnb.
angel-fallabrino-sa.flagship_grapes: 100% Tannat; top red of the Don Angelo VCP (Vino de Calidad Preferente) range, 14.5% abv, released for the winery's centenary.

antigua-bodega.history: The winery states that it was built in 1928 in Santos Lugares, La Paz. In 1955 the marriage of Héctor Nelson Stagnari and Mariana Moise united two families on that property. Today it is run by Virginia Stagnari, the fifth generation, with her children Mariana, a winemaker, and Carlo, who is in charge of the vineyard.
highlights: Subsoil of decomposed pink granite ('granito de La Paz'), 500-600 million years old, according to the winery.
30 ha of its own between Santos Lugares (La Paz) and Melilla, by the Santa Lucía River.
Run by the fifth and sixth generations: Virginia Stagnari and her children Mariana and Carlo.
antigua-bodega.flagship_grapes: 100% Tannat from Riberas del Santa Lucía (Santos Lugares, Canelones); red aged in French and American oak barrels.

areosa-oscar-raul.history: Producer registered with INAVI under the name of Oscar Raúl Areosa, in Rincón del Cerro, in the rural west of Montevideo. The official listing publishes only an address, a map and contact details.

aromas-del-sur.history: Winery of the Morando family in Juanicó, Canelones, on Ruta 5. According to INAVI, it makes table wines from its own grapes, which it sells on the Uruguayan market, to other wineries and for export.
highlights: Table wines from its own grapes in Juanicó; sells to other wineries and exports, according to INAVI.
aromas-del-sur.flagship_grapes: Family table wine, in a 1 L bottle and a 3 L bag-in-box.

artesana-winery.history: American businessman Blake Heinemann discovered Uruguayan Tannat in 2003 and in 2007 founded Artesana with his family and winemaker Analía Lazaneo. In 2007 and 2008 they planted Tannat, Merlot and Zinfandel in Las Brujas, Canelones; they later added Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay and Petit Manseng.
highlights: According to the winery, it makes the first and only Zinfandel in Uruguay.
8.5 ha of vineyards in 13 plots on calcareous clay soils, according to SAWG.
Uruguay's Winery of the Year at the 2017 New York International Wine Competition, according to SAWG.
artesana-winery.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat, Zinfandel and Merlot (percentages not published); red with 18 to 24 months in oak barrels.

atlantica-gourmet-srl.history: Bodega Atlántica was launched in 2019, founded by Adriana Fernández, as a boutique brand of limited-batch wines with labels designed by visual artists. It owns no vineyards: it selects grapes from Canelones, San José, Salto and Maldonado depending on the variety, working with winemaker Fernando Pettenuzzo. It is registered with INAVI as Atlántica Gourmet SRL, with a declared facility in San José.
highlights: Founded in 2019 by Adriana Fernández; winemaker Fernando Pettenuzzo, trained in Uruguay, Champagne and Catalonia
No estate vineyard: buys grapes in Canelones, San José, Salto and Maldonado depending on the variety
Six wines from five varieties: Albariño, Tannat, Malbec, Sauvignon Blanc sur lie and a Cabernet Franc blend
atlantica-gourmet-srl.flagship_grapes: 100% Albariño from Canelones; fresh white with marked acidity and notes of citrus and white flowers

avisara-sa.history: Avisara SA appears in the INAVI winery registry with a facility at Ruta 6 km 29.800, Canelones. It shares its address, telephone and contact email with Adarel SA, another company registered with INAVI. No website, commercial brand or published information about its wines was found.
highlights: Shares its INAVI address and contact details with Adarel SA (Ruta 6 km 29.800, Sauce)

bentancor-y-cia-sci.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Bentancor y Cía. SCI, in rural Montevideo. The official listing publishes only an address, a map and contact details.

beretta-bodega-y-vinedos.history: Family winery in Melilla, in the rural area of Montevideo, with a tradition dating back to 1913, when Italian immigrant Antonio Beretta settled in the area. It remains in family hands and makes fine and table wines from its own grapes and from neighboring vineyards in the south of the country, combining traditional methods with current technology.
highlights: Family tradition since 1913, begun by Italian immigrant Antonio Beretta.
Makes fine and table wines from estate and purchased grapes from the south of the country, according to INAVI.
Offers a shop and tasting tours in Melilla.
beretta-bodega-y-vinedos.flagship_grapes: Label of the Leticia Villalba brand, from Bodega Beretta; the winery does not publish the grape varieties.

bertolini-y-broglio.history: Boutique winery founded in 1998 as a family project on Ruta 3 km 468.5, in the Daymán area on the border between Paysandú and Salto, managed from Salto. In 2015 it had a capacity of 60,000 to 65,000 liters per year and produced Tannat, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, as well as a small plot of Carménère, which is rare in Uruguay. Agronomist Juan Pedro Broglio is its winemaker and physician Luis Batlle Bertolini is listed as the winery's principal; its wines are sold in supermarkets and wine shops.
highlights: One of the few wineries registered with INAVI in the department of Salto.
Offers a shop and tasting tours, according to INAVI.
bertolini-y-broglio.flagship_grapes: High-end Tannat, in two versions that shops call Americano and Francés.

blanco-zanola-claro-blanco.history: Producer registered with INAVI under the name of Claro Juan Blanco Zanola, on Ruta 6 in Sauce, Canelones. The official listing publishes only an address, a map and contact details.

bodega-ariano.history: Family winery founded in 1929 by Italian immigrants in El Colorado, Canelones, about 20 km from the port of Montevideo. Today it is run by the fourth generation of the Ariano family under the company name Ariano Hnos. SA; it sells on the domestic market and exports, and receives guided visits with direct sales.
highlights: Founded in 1929 by Italian immigrants; fourth generation at the helm, according to INAVI.
Located about 20 km from the port of Montevideo, on Ruta 48 in El Colorado.
Offers guided visits and a shop, and exports its wines, according to INAVI.

bodega-atlantida-sa.history: Winery on Ruta 11, in the Atlántida area of Canelones, producing Tannat, Viognier, Verdello and sparkling wines. Its Tannat Reserva 2016, aged 12 months in French and American oak, won a silver medal at the 2018 New York International Wine Competition, where the winery was named Uruguay Winery of the Year.
highlights: Silver medal for the Tannat Reserva 2016 at the 2018 New York International Wine Competition.
Named 'Uruguay Winery of the Year' 2018 at that same competition, according to the winery.
Vineyards on wind-exposed slopes close to the ocean, according to the winery's own description.
bodega-atlantida-sa.flagship_grapes: Tannat; hand-harvested, 12 months in French and American oak barrels (2016 vintage, 13.9% abv)

bodega-baceda.history: Family winery registered with INAVI in Santos Lugares, Canelones, under the names of Hugo Marcelo Baceda Caraballo and Sonia Castagnino Seris. The official listing publishes only an address, a map and contact details.

bodega-bouza.history: The Bouza family entered the wine business in 1998 by buying a 35-year-old vineyard in Las Violetas, Canelones. In 2001 it acquired a property in Melilla with a winery that had operated in the 1950s and 1960s, and restored it. Winemaker Eduardo Boido heads the winery, which works only with its own grapes.
highlights: Five estate vineyards across Montevideo, Canelones and Maldonado; the Las Espinas vineyard is 3 km from the sea.
It planted its first hectare of Albariño in 2001 and harvested it for the first time in 2004.
Las Espinas (Punta Negra): stony trachyte soils of low fertility and very good drainage, according to the winery.
bodega-bouza.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat, Merlot and Tempranillo (2018 vintage: 45/35/20); barrel-selection red aged in oak; the Merlot and Tempranillo are blended together before joining the Tannat.

bodega-bresesti.history: Small family-run, artisanal winery founded in 1937 by immigrants from northern Italy and now run by the third and fourth generations of the Bresesti family. It vinifies in old concrete vats that have seen more than 80 harvests and, since around 2015, has crushed by gravity with a restored crusher; it describes itself as a boutique winery of small varietal collections.
highlights: Founded in 1937; third and fourth generations in charge, according to INAVI and the official website.
More than 40 labels in small collections, with Arinarnoa, Cabernet Franc and Tannat among its varietals.
Vinifies in historic concrete vats and crushes by gravity with a restored machine.
bodega-bresesti.flagship_grapes: Varietal Tannat, the highest-tier label in the official shop (Premium line, also available in magnum and gift box).

bodega-brisas.history: Winery of businessman Alejandro Bulgheroni in Altos de José Ignacio, Maldonado, with the first vineyards planted in 2012 and the winery completed in 2019. The estate covers 325 hectares, 80 of them under vine, and the winery has a capacity of five million liters, geared toward efficiently produced wines with mechanized harvesting. The winemaker is Germán Bruzzone, who also makes the wines at Bodega Garzón.
highlights: 80 hectares of vineyard on a 325 ha estate; 7,226 m² winery completed in 2019.
Altos de José Ignacio Tannat Reserva 2017: 93 points from Decanter and bronze at the Sommelier Wine Awards.
Vineyards on coastal slopes with constant Atlantic breezes; 100% mechanized harvest.
bodega-brisas.flagship_grapes: Tannat with nearly a year in barrel; export range. 93 points from Decanter for the 2017 vintage

bodega-campotinto.history: Winery with an inn and restaurant in Colonia Estrella, in the Carmelo area, where Italian and French-Basque settlers have grown vines for more than a century. According to El Observador (2020), Casona Campotinto offers tastings and picnics among the vineyards, and the inn has 12 rooms opposite the San Roque chapel, with a restaurant serving Italian and Uruguayan cuisine open to the public.
highlights: 12-room inn among the vineyards, opposite the San Roque chapel in Colonia Estrella.
Restaurant open to the public with Italian and Uruguayan cuisine, according to El Observador (2020).
Located opposite Bodega Cordano - Almacén de la Capilla, in the same Colonia Estrella area.
bodega-campotinto.flagship_grapes: Red blend; the winery works with Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Marselan, Viognier, Muscat and Ugni Blanc.

bodega-canaparro.history: Winery of the Canaparro family in Manga, in rural Montevideo, founded in 1964. According to INAVI, it has made its wines exclusively from estate-grown grapes ever since.
highlights: Founded in 1964; makes wine only from estate-grown grapes, according to INAVI.
bodega-canaparro.flagship_grapes: Sweet rosé, labeled as "Vino Natural"; the source does not state the grape.

bodega-caprile.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Caprile Hnos. SRL, on Avenida Pedro de Mendoza in rural Montevideo, a few blocks from Bodega Valdi. The official listing publishes only an address, a map and contact details.

bodega-carrasco.history: Winery of the Charamelo family on Ruta 33, in Carrasco del Sauce (Canelones).

bodega-cattani.history: Winery in Salto, with the legal name Mensah SRL, listed by the Centro Comercial e Industrial de Salto as a wine producer and beverage distributor with premises at Rivera 1789. Its website presents a new winery on Ruta 3 km 481.5, a few kilometers from the city. The Salto municipal government lists it as Bodega Cattani-Orihuela, with about 20,000 liters of production from French varieties. It makes Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, a blend of the three and the Tannat Madera, from grapes harvested at different levels of ripeness.
highlights: Salto winery of about 20,000 liters
Wines from overripe grapes, in the Salto style
Tannat Madera with 12 months in oak
bodega-cattani.flagship_grapes: Tannat from overripe grapes with 12 months in oak barrels.

bodega-cerro-chapeu.history: The Carrau family, with a winemaking tradition dating back to 1752 in Catalonia and to 1930 in Uruguay, planted the first vineyards at Cerro Chapeu in 1975 and pioneered wine in Rivera. In 1997 it built a gravity-flow winery dug into the hillside. It produces the Castel Pujol, Cerro Chapeu, Batovi, 1752 Gran Tradición, Ysern and Sust ranges.
highlights: Deep red sandy soils with high iron content and good drainage, according to the winery.
Gravity-flow winery from 1997 dug four levels into the hillside, with no pumps in the cellar.
Wine tourism experience from Thursday to Sunday; part of the estate lies in Brazilian territory.
bodega-cerro-chapeu.flagship_grapes: Single-vineyard Tannat from the oldest plot on the estate, clone 1

bodega-cerro-del-toro-sa.history: A project of the Japanese Kambara family, who in the 1980s bought an 800-hectare property in Piriápolis that includes Cerro del Toro. They planted the first vines in the spring of 2016 and today have 28 hectares, near where Francisco Piria had vineyards in the early 20th century.
highlights: Vineyard about 2 km as the crow flies from the beaches of Piriápolis, between 50 and 120 m.
Stony soils with granite, quartz and limestone rock; calcium carbonate at mid-depth.
Its Alquimia Corte Único Blanco 2021 was Uruguay's best white wine in Descorchados 2022.

bodega-cis.history: Winery on Cerro de Carmelo (Colonia), about 5 km from the town. The family arrived with Adolfo Cis, an immigrant from Trento who settled in the area in 1896; in 1918 Rodolfo Cis and María Zelmira Pérez founded the winery, first called Granja Villa Teresa, and planted Tannat (Harriague), Folle Noir (Vidiella) and Muscat of Hamburg. After the death of Rodolfo Cis, his children continued the business. It has 3 ha of vineyard with Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Tannat, Chardonnay, Viognier and Muscat of Hamburg, and a capacity to process 150,000 kg of grapes per year.
highlights: Part of the core group of small wineries in Carmelo, in southwestern Colonia.
bodega-cis.flagship_grapes: Rosé of Muscat of Hamburg, the wine that defined Rodolfo Cis's style according to the winery's history.

bodega-d-mozzo.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the name of Diego Martín Mozzo Sabato, on Ruta 48 in El Colorado, Canelones, a traditional vineyard area near Las Brujas. No website, social media or press coverage were found to expand the profile.

bodega-dante-villarino.history: According to Placer magazine (2007), the Villarino family has been settled in Sauce (Canelones) since 1801, has made wine since 1888, and the current winery dates from 1954, with Dante Villarino at the helm and much of the family working in it. It had about 22 hectares of vineyard on Ruta 33, opposite the winery, with Tannat, Merlot and Syrah, and a capacity of 550,000 liters. Its Merlot held national organic certification from ARU and the labels featured paintings by Diego Massi.
highlights: Family in Sauce since 1801 and making wine since 1888
Merlot with national organic certification (ARU)
Labels featuring paintings by Diego Massi
bodega-dante-villarino.flagship_grapes: Merlot from a vineyard with national organic certification (ARU), on the slope of the Cuchilla Grande, Sauce.

bodega-don-pose.history: Small winery in the rural Melilla area, in the northwest of Montevideo, registered with INAVI. Vivino lists four non-vintage wines: an Arinarnoa, a Moscato Giallo, a Tannat and a blend called Blend de Lorena. No website or press coverage about its history was found.
highlights: Makes a varietal Arinarnoa, a Tannat x Cabernet Sauvignon cross that is rare in Uruguay.

bodega-duran-zambelli.history: Family winery of the Durán family in Canelón Chico (Ruta 69 km 28.5), with a vineyard in the Santos Lugares area. It makes its wines by hand and took part in Canelones' Fiesta Capital de la Uva y el Vino in 2023.
highlights: Four generations in viticulture
Own winery since 2010
Tinto Tannat as its flagship wine
bodega-duran-zambelli.flagship_grapes: Tannat, a red sold in one-litre bottles; the website presents it as its flagship wine.

bodega-el-chaparral.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Colinas del Sur SA, located at Fuster and Ruta 64, on the outskirts of the city of Canelones. The official listing reports only a shop and contact details.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop at Fuster and Ruta 64, Canelones.

bodega-eliseo-argentino.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Eliseo Argentino Ltda., located on Ruta 5 near Progreso, in the Canelones wine belt. No website, social media or press coverage were found that would allow its history or production to be reconstructed.

bodega-etcheverry.history: In 1960 Juan Francisco Etcheverry bought the first 6 hectares on the banks of the Arroyo Gigante, in Progreso, and planted the first vineyards; in 1976 he founded the winery on that property. In 1989 the vineyards were replanted with certified plant material of French origin. Today the company (Provemax S.A.) farms 40 hectares of its own and produces table and fine wines.
highlights: Founded in 1976 on a property bought in 1960 by Juan Francisco Etcheverry.
Vineyards replanted in 1989 with certified material of French origin.
40 estate hectares trained on an open lyre system, as the winery describes on INAVI.
bodega-etcheverry.flagship_grapes: Tannat; red with time in oak barrels.

bodega-familia-barbero.history: Family winery in Melilla (Montevideo), with the legal name Lamitel SA, which presents itself as three generations of winemakers. It makes a short range of varietal wines (Chardonnay, Merlot, Merlot rosé, Tannat, Tannat Roble Reserva and a Tannat-Merlot bivarietal) and light, low-alcohol drinks such as Solo 4 and a strawberry one. It sells directly from the winery, through its website and on WhatsApp, and has an events hall with tastings.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop in the Melilla wine-growing area, Montevideo.
bodega-familia-barbero.flagship_grapes: Tannat aged in oak; it is the Reserva label of a short range of varietal wines.

familia-irurtia.history: Lorenzo Irurtia, a Basque immigrant, began planting vines in the Carmelo area around 1913, and the winery was formally established in 1940. His grandson Dante ran it for 56 vintages. In March 2026 the industrial property went to a court-ordered auction and was bought by BROU, its main creditor.
highlights: Dante Irurtia, the founder's grandson, led 56 vintages; afterwards the fourth generation took over.
It produced about one million liters a year, according to El Observador (2020).
In March 2026 BROU bought the winery's property at a court-ordered auction for US$750,000.
familia-irurtia.flagship_grapes: Tannat; oak-aged red from the Reserva del Virrey range, Dante Irurtia brand.

bodega-familia-moizo.history: Family and artisanal winery in Canelones, founded in 1954 according to the Catraca Livre guide, which follows the Piedmontese winemaking tradition. Visits are personalized, led by winemakers from the family itself, and include a tour of the vineyards and the old winery, a tasting and home-cooked food. It holds an annual Tannat and Lamb event.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop, tasting tours and occasional events.
Located on Ruta 5 in Progreso, a traditional wine-growing area of Canelones.
bodega-familia-moizo.flagship_grapes: Tannat; red wine aged in oak from the Reserva Privada line.

bodega-favretto.history: Bodega Favretto operates under the Favretto Dragone brand, after the surnames of its founders (Luis Favretto and Medarda Dragone), at Ruta 75 km 37, Costa de Pando (Canelones). Today it is run by the five Favretto-Dragone siblings, the fourth generation at the winery; the grandparents' wine was called 'Margarita', after the nonna. It makes reds, whites, rosés and sparkling wines, sold in Uruguayan shops, and in 2024 it redesigned its labels with the Mendoza studio Dizen.
highlights: Fourth family generation in Costa de Pando
Labels redesigned in 2024 (Dizen, Mendoza)
Reserva line with 18 months in oak
bodega-favretto.flagship_grapes: Varietal Tannat with 18 months in American oak, from Costa de Pando (Canelones); notes of vanilla, chocolate, tobacco, fig and plum.

bodega-filgueira.history: Family vineyard of the Filgueira family in Santa Lucía (Canelones). According to Guru'Guay (2018), the parents of Manuel Filgueira, physicians by profession, ran the winery and took it from table wine to quality wine, with advice from Bordeaux winemaker Jean-Pascal Lacaze; in 2010 they decided to sell the vineyard. Manuel, the family's fourth generation, kept his share and continued making wine with his own project, Los Nadies.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a restaurant, shop, tasting tours and events.
Located in the Santa Lucía area, northwest of Canelones, on Ruta 81.

bodega-fripp.history: The Fripp family has grown grapes in Carmelo (Colonia) since the 1970s, with the same vines still in production. Leandro Fripp started the winery in 2008, at the age of 17, with makeshift equipment, and in 2018 he undertook the conversion of the estate inherited from his father, reorienting it toward wine tourism; his brother takes care of the vineyard work. They went from producing about 200,000 liters of bulk table wine to a premium line called Ilusión, of about 12,000 bottles sold in their own restaurant. The vineyard has 4 hectares planted to Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Marselan.
highlights: Family business registered with INAVI with a shop and tasting tours.
bodega-fripp.flagship_grapes: Tannat; red wine from the premium Ilusión line.

bodega-garaje-casa-grande-arte-vina.history: Family garage winery in Rincón de Carrasco, Canelones, whose origins go back to the vineyard that Italian immigrant Gaetano De Maio started in the 1920s; today it is run by the fourth generation under the company name Arte y Viña SRL. It makes small lots in the Joven Artística, Artística Reserva and Píccola ranges and receives visitors from Monday to Saturday.
highlights: Origins in Gaetano De Maio's vineyard in the 1920s; fourth family generation.
Super Blend Tinto with 18 months in barrel and Gran Tannacito with 14, according to the official website.
Tastings with a tour of the vineyard, winery and cellar, Monday to Saturday.
bodega-garaje-casa-grande-arte-vina.flagship_grapes: Blend of six red varieties; 18 months in barrel.

bodega-garzon.history: A project of Alejandro P. Bulgheroni and his wife Bettina in the hills of Garzón. The first plantings date from 2007-2008, the first harvest from 2010, and the winery, built in terraces on the hillside, opened in March 2016.
highlights: According to the winery, it is the first sustainable winery outside North America with LEED certification.
Named New World Winery of the Year 2018 by Wine Enthusiast magazine.
More than 1,000 plots on balasto soils, about 18 km from the Atlantic.
bodega-garzon.flagship_grapes: Tannat, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot and Marselan (blend; proportions may vary by vintage)

bodega-j-chiappella.history: The Chiappella family came to Uruguay from Piedmont around 1926 and settled in Cuchilla de Rocha, Canelones. In 1959 three brothers bought the current property, and in 1988 Jesús Chiappella acquired the winery and vineyards and began the conversion to fine varieties, continued by his winemaker daughters Laura and Karina.
highlights: 40 hectares of vineyard around the winery, 30 km from central Montevideo.
Makes a Muscat of Hamburg Mistela from an Italian family recipe (El Observador, 2013).
Winemakers Laura and Karina Chiappella, who qualified in 2002; the vineyard is worked by Juan Jesús and Juan Martín.
bodega-j-chiappella.flagship_grapes: Blend of seven varieties in equal parts (about 14% each) from estate vineyards in Cuchilla de Rocha, with 9 months in barrel.

bodega-leonardo-falcone.history: Family winery in Paysandú founded by an Italian family who arrived in the region in 1886; according to the family, that year 'grandfather Domingo' gave the venture its name. Today it is run by the third and fourth generations, with winemaker Carolina Falcone in charge of production.
highlights: Abuelo Domingo Tannat 2022: Gold Medal at Vinalies 2023 (Œnologues de France).
One of the four winning projects of the Ministry of Tourism's first competitive Wine Tourism Fund (2022).
Vineyards on clay-limestone soils trained on a lyre system, according to South America Wine Guide.
bodega-leonardo-falcone.flagship_grapes: Tannat, a tribute to the winery's founder.

bodega-lugano.history: Bodega y Viñedos Lugano is located on Ruta 11 km 97, in Canelones, with the legal name Ticigal S.A. Its packaging bears the legend 'Desde 1915' and it sells wines in cartons, such as a Tinto Abocado Tannat-Merlot and a Rosado Abocado Moscatel.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop on Ruta 11, Canelones.

bodega-maua.history: Winery located beside Castillo Mauá, the estancia house that the Baron of Mauá, the Brazilian businessman Irineu Evangelista de Sousa, had built around 1857 on the banks of the Río Negro, near Mercedes. According to El Observador (2013), the old winery adjoining the castle still produces wines known in the local Mercedes circuit.
highlights: Winery adjoining Castillo Mauá (c. 1857), the Baron of Mauá's house on the banks of the Río Negro.
The castle building now belongs to the Intendencia de Soriano, according to Welcome Uruguay.
Stores wine in French oak barrels and casks, according to a visit report by Welcome Uruguay.
bodega-maua.flagship_grapes: Medium-sweet frizzante Chardonnay: a lightly sparkling white with body and fruity aromas.

bodega-mederos.history: Family winery in Sauce, Canelones, registered with INAVI under the name of Alberto Mederos, on Ruta 33 km 33. It markets wines under the Bodega Mederos brand: Tannat, Tannat Reserva, a Tannat blend and an Albariño.
highlights: Makes Tannat, Tannat Reserva, a Tannat blend and Albariño under the Bodega Mederos brand.

bodega-miguel-francone.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the name of Miguel Ángel Francone Zanolla, in the rural Colón-Melilla area in the northwest of Montevideo. No website, social media or press coverage were found to expand the profile.

bodega-molinari.history: Bodega Molinari is registered with INAVI under the company name Marino Molinari e Hijos SRL, with a winery at Ruta 5 km 36.500, Canelones, on the historic Ruta 5 wine corridor. No website or published information about its history, vineyards or wines was found.
highlights: Company name Marino Molinari e Hijos SRL, according to the INAVI registry

bodega-nabune.history: Family winery in Las Piedras (Canelones) of Italian origin: the maternal grandfather Roberto Sciutti moved from the farm plot to the vineyard and to wine, and Carlos Nabune, married to Sonia Sciutti, leased the winery around the year 2000. It is now run by the Nabune family with the siblings Gerardo (winemaker), Gustavo and Cecilia; it has 22 hectares of irrigated vineyard and in 2007 it bought another small winery with 8 hectares near La Paz. It produces about 600,000 liters of table wine per year (demijohn and Tetra Brik, El Nogal brand) and slightly more than 25,000 bottles of fine wine.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop in Las Piedras, Canelones.
bodega-nabune.flagship_grapes: Blend of Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Tannat, the latter with a brief spell in barrel; the percentages vary each year.

bodega-oceanica-jose-ignacio.history: Winery on an estate of about 50 hectares near José Ignacio that combines vineyard, olive grove and the O'33 olive oil mill. The vines, about 8 hectares, were planted in 2012 less than 500 meters from the winery. The wines are made by winemaker Hans Vinding-Diers.
highlights: Vineyards less than 500 m from the winery, on silt-loam soils over crystalline basement.
Ultramar line: bottles aged underwater at a depth of 15 meters in the Atlantic off José Ignacio.
Descorchados 2019 named its Albariño 2018 Uruguay's best white wine.
bodega-oceanica-jose-ignacio.flagship_grapes: Albariño; white fermented in stainless steel, fresh, with saline notes.

bodega-pablo-fallabrino.history: Angelo Fallabrino, Pablo's grandfather, arrived from Piedmont in 1920 and in the 1930s planted five vineyards and opened two wineries. Pablo Fallabrino, who learned the trade from his father and grandfather, started the current vineyard in Atlántida in 1997; it was marketed as Viñedo de los Vientos and now bears his name.
highlights: Vineyard on the windy rolling hills of Atlántida, about 4 km from the sea, according to its importer.
It mainly plants Piedmontese varieties, such as Nebbiolo, as well as Tannat.
It makes Alcyone, a non-vintage dessert Tannat, and a sulfite-free Tannat (Anarkia).

bodega-parodi.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the name of María Teresita Parodi, on Ruta 6 in Santa Rosa, in the east of the department of Canelones. No website, social media or press coverage were found that would allow its history or production to be reconstructed.

bodega-quinta-santero.history: Since 1950 the Santero family has made wine in an artisanal way in Sauce (Canelones), and the practice has been passed down to the fourth generation, now running the winery. It makes varietal wines from Tannat, Marselan, Cabernet Sauvignon and Gewürztraminer, with oaked versions of Tannat and Marselan, as well as blends such as El Tesoro Blend, Cosecha Única and Lorena. It also has a Zenit line of fruit-based drinks (passion fruit, frizzante mango, native fruits).
highlights: Among its highest-rated labels on Vivino are an oaked Marselan and an oaked Tannat.
In addition to wines, it sells a Zenit line of fruit-based drinks (passion fruit, mango, native fruits).
bodega-quinta-santero.flagship_grapes: Marselan; red wine with oak aging.

bodega-roses.history: Family business founded in 1977 in Sauce, Canelones, by Jacinto Rosés and Melva Martínez together with their sons Jaime, Walter and Pablo; the third generation has already joined. According to INAVI, it has gradually expanded production and planted vineyards in several regions of the country, and recently launched a line of fine wines.
highlights: Founded in 1977; the third generation of the Rosés family has joined.
Vineyards in several regions of the country and sales in various types of packaging, according to INAVI.
Recent line of fine wines with international awards, according to INAVI (no details given).
bodega-roses.flagship_grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Gran Reserva level (2011 vintage in the listing).

bodega-rovere.history: Small family winery in the rural locality of Bañado, San José, whose origins go back to the paternal great-grandfather of the Rovere family, who emigrated from Italy; today it is run by the fourth generation under the company name La Geovana Ltda. It has a capacity of nearly 370,000 liters and offers a shop, tasting tours and events.
highlights: Fourth generation of a family of Italian origin, according to INAVI.
Vessel capacity of nearly 370,000 liters, according to INAVI.
Offers a shop, tasting tours and occasional events.
bodega-rovere.flagship_grapes: Tannat; Vino de Calidad Preferente (VCP), Uruguay's quality-wine category.

bodega-salto-chico.history: Boutique vineyard and winery in Colonia Osimani, on the bank of the Uruguay River north of the city of Salto, facing the Salto Chico rapids that give it its name. The vines were planted from 1999 onward in the department where Pascual Harriague introduced Tannat in the 19th century.
highlights: Soils of sand and rounded pebbles left by an ancient bed of the Uruguay River, according to the winery.
Irrigated when necessary with natural mineral water from two wells; hand-harvested.
Tannat Reserva 2007: Gold Medal at Vinalies Internationales 2011 (Paris), according to the winery.

bodega-san-jacinto.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Suryfell S.A., on Ruta 7 in San Jacinto, in eastern Canelones. No website, social media or press coverage was found that would allow its history or production to be reconstructed.
bodega-san-jacinto.flagship_grapes: Red blend of Merlot and Tannat.

bodega-santa-rosa.history: According to its WineTourism.com profile, Juan Bautista Passadore founded the winery in 1898 and eight generations have run it. Bodegas Carrau states that Catalan winemaker Juan Carrau Sust, who arrived in 1930, took part in founding Santa Rosa during that decade. It preserves underground cellars that can be visited on guided tours.
highlights: Underground cellars that the winery describes as among the largest in operation in South America.
Guided tour with museum and tasting, in Spanish, English and Portuguese.
bodega-santa-rosa.flagship_grapes: Traditional-method sparkling wine, with secondary fermentation in the bottle.

bodega-sierra-oriental.history: Boutique winery created by businessman Rodrigo Diz Solari in Las Cañas, Maldonado, near the source of the José Ignacio stream and 32 km from the Atlantic, with vineyards planted in 2003. It has 9 hectares of vines (Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Sauvignon Blanc, Sangiovese and Pinot Grigio) and aims at no more than 30,000 bottles per year. Winemaking was handled by Juan Andrés Marichal and, since 2020, by Gastón Vitale; its main point of sale is Iberpark.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop and tasting tours in the hill country of Maldonado.
bodega-sierra-oriental.flagship_grapes: Tannat from its own vineyards in Las Cañas, near José Ignacio (Maldonado).

bodega-sin-nombre.history: Small winery in Canelón Chico (Canelones) whose owner, Alberto Luis Plata, is engaged in supplying inputs for dairy farming and importing inputs for the wine industry. In 2004 he planted a couple of hectares of vines on his small farm and set up his own winery; the legal name is Agro Abastecimientos SRL.
highlights: Makes a varietal Caladoc, a cross of Grenache and Malbec that is little known in Uruguay.
bodega-sin-nombre.flagship_grapes: Caladoc (a cross of Grenache and Malbec); varietal red wine from Canelones.

bodega-spinoglio.history: Luigi Spinoglio, from Casale Monferrato (Piedmont), arrived in Uruguay in the late 19th century. In 1961 his grandson Ángel took over the estate in Cuchilla Pereyra that José Campomar had started in 1898. Today it is run by Diego Spinoglio, the fourth generation of the family in Uruguay.
highlights: It preserves a plot of century-old vines as viticultural heritage, according to the winery.
Stone-walled cellar, built bearing the hallmark of French master builders.
It offers guided tours, tastings, the MonfrÀ restaurant and lodging on the estate.
bodega-spinoglio.flagship_grapes: Tannat from the best plots of each vintage, barrel selection; red aged in oak (duration not published).

bodega-tomasi.history: Winery with a family tradition dating back to 1942 in Rincón del Cerro, in the rural west of Montevideo, now run by Carlos Tomasi. In 1999 he and winemaker Juan Ferreri bought a farm near Lomas de la Paloma, Rocha, where he grows 11 hectares of vines; his fine wines (Dominio Cassis brand) come from there, while the table wines come from Montevideo.
highlights: Family tradition since 1942 in Rincón del Cerro, Montevideo.
11-hectare vineyard in Rocha, near Lomas de la Paloma, with seven red and two white varieties.
Its fine wines are sold as Dominio Cassis; the table wines are made from Montevideo grapes.
bodega-tomasi.flagship_grapes: Tannat clone 717 from Rocha, 18 months in French oak (2016 vintage reviewed by Catadores)

bodega-tres-puentes.history: Small winery in the city of Treinta y Tres that makes artisanal fruity wines, produced by Andrés González according to its labels and brochure. It sells in bottles and larger containers, and takes part in fairs with its own stand.
highlights: One of the few wineries registered with INAVI in the department of Treinta y Tres.
bodega-tres-puentes.flagship_grapes: Line of artisanal fruity wines: wine with peach, orange, pear, apple, strawberry and pineapple.

bodega-trombotti.history: Family winery registered with INAVI under the name of Luis Alberto Trombotti Souto, on Ruta 8 near Pando, in the south of Canelones. Vivino lists a single wine, a Tannat. No website or press coverage about its history was found.

bodega-turistica-los-pinos.history: Artisanal winery in Nueva Helvecia, Colonia, which according to INAVI is a hundred years old and has belonged since 1965 to the families of Rogelio Ingold and Carlos Moreda, today represented by Julio Ingold, Mirta Rivas and Gladys Vonrotz. It opened to visitors on 20 October 2019 with guided tours of the vineyard, machine room and cellar centered on the family history.
highlights: Centenary winery according to INAVI; owned by the Ingold and Moreda families since 1965.
Open for wine tourism since 20 October 2019, with guided tours and a shop.
Located in Nueva Helvecia, a Swiss-founded colony in the department of Colonia.
bodega-turistica-los-pinos.flagship_grapes: Tannat; the winery says it focuses on its Tannats, named after episodes of the family history.

bodega-valdi.history: Family company in rural Montevideo, in the Peñarol Viejo and Cuchilla Pereira area, which according to INAVI descends from an Italian family that arrived some five generations ago and began planting vineyards in 1892. It makes artisanal wines, grappa and liqueurs, with a tradition passed down from parents to children.
highlights: Family of Italian origin with vineyards planted since 1892, according to INAVI.
Some five generations in the trade; makes artisanal wines, grappa and liqueurs.
bodega-valdi.flagship_grapes: Tannat; Vino de Calidad Preferente (VCP) from the reserva range.

bodega-wasiluk.history: Family winery in Paysandú (Bodega Wasiluk Ltda.) located on Ruta 90, km 9. In July 2010 it was, together with Falcone, the host winery of the third Paysandú Wine Tasting, with the whole family present; El Telégrafo was still naming it in 2024 among the active wineries of the department.
highlights: One of the few wineries registered in Paysandú, in the northern littoral on the Uruguay River.

bodega-y-vinedos-bandelli.history: Family winery founded in 1930 in Punta de Rieles (Montevideo). It makes and distributes artisanal wine with home delivery.

bodega-y-vinedos-cordano-almacen-de-la-c.history: Family winery in Colonia Estrella, Carmelo, which presents a family tradition dating back to 1855 and is now run by Diego Vecchio and Ana Paula Cordano, fifth generation of winemakers. It farms about 8 hectares with a production of close to 15,000 bottles a year and operates alongside the Almacén de la Capilla, a country general store with visits, a shop and a cabin among the vineyards.
highlights: Fifth generation of winemakers; '5ta Generación' range with Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat-Merlot and Syrah.
About 8 hectares and close to 15,000 bottles a year, according to El Observador (2020).
Located opposite the Casona Campotinto, in the historic wine district of Colonia Estrella.
bodega-y-vinedos-cordano-almacen-de-la-c.flagship_grapes: Sweet, refreshing, lightly sparkling wine; also available as a 'medio y medio'

bodega-zubizarreta.history: Family winery in Carmelo that has made wine since 1957, started by a Basque immigrant whose family settled on the lands of the old Calera de las Huérfanas. Today it is run by the third generation of the Zubizarreta-Menna family. The Casa de Aitona, an early 20th-century manor house restored in 2001, was opened to wine tourism together with the winery.
highlights: Third generation of a family of Basque origin; has made wine in Carmelo since 1957.
40 hectares of vineyard with Tannat, Marselan, Arinarnoa, Cabernet, Merlot, Albariño and Sauvignon Blanc.
Sandy loam soils and a microclimate with wide day-night temperature swings thanks to the nearby Río de la Plata, according to the winery.
bodega-zubizarreta.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat and Marselan; El Observador presents it as the flagship wine. The Alta Gama range also includes varietal Tannat, Marselan and Albariño

bodegas-carrau.history: The Carrau family bought its first vineyard in Vilassar de Mar, Catalonia, in 1752. In 1930 winemaker Juan Carrau Sust emigrated to Uruguay with his family. In 1976 Bodegas Carrau was created to export Uruguayan wine, with the purchase of Pablo Varzi's winery, founded in 1887.
highlights: Ten generations of grape growers; the family's first vineyard was bought in Vilassar de Mar in 1752.
It operates in Pablo Varzi's former winery (1887); the project was declared of National Interest in 1977.
Cerro Chapeu (Rivera) is now the winery of another branch of the Carrau family and holds old Tannat clones.
bodegas-carrau.flagship_grapes: 100% Tannat from estate vineyards in Cerro Chapeu (Rivera), sandy soils; red aged in French oak barrels.

bodega-castillo-viejo.history: The Etcheverry family, originally from Hasparren in the French Basque Country, founded the winery in 1927 in Las Piedras; Uruguay XXI credits Santos Etcheverry with the founding. Today it is run by the third and fourth generations, who make wine from grapes from their own vineyards and from selected growers in different regions of the country.
highlights: El Preciado scored 93 points in Descorchados 2021, according to the Uruguay XXI profile.
Catamayor Reserva de Familia Tannat 2017: 92 points in Descorchados 2021.
It works with grapes from sandy, calcareous, clay, clay-loam and granitic soils, according to the winery.
bodega-castillo-viejo.flagship_grapes: The house's top-of-the-range red blend; the sources consulted do not publish its composition or aging. Descorchados 2021 includes it in its ranking of best reds with 93 points.

bodegas-valente-ltda.history: Winery registered with INAVI as Bodegas Valente Ltda., in Peñarol Viejo, in the rural area of northeastern Montevideo. No website, social media or press coverage were found that would allow its history or production to be reconstructed.
bodegas-valente-ltda.flagship_grapes: Tannat and Merlot blend; table wine in 1 L packaging. There is also a semi-sweet white Muscat.

braccobosca-winery.history: The Bracco family, of Piedmontese origin, settled in the Atlántida area and has grown vines there for five generations. Darwin Bracco and Mirtha Bosca bought the property known as 'Gallegos', which already had vineyards, and the winery was founded in 2005. Today it is run by Fabiana Bracco.
highlights: About 8 km from the sea, in an ecologically protected area next to Laguna del Cisne.
Clay, limestone and silt soils with plenty of quartz, according to Fabiana Bracco (Forbes, 2025).
Named 'Winery of the Year' by the Descorchados guide, according to Forbes (April 2025).

bruzzone-y-sciutto.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Bruzzone y Sciutto S.A., located on Camino Guerra, in the Manga area in the east of Montevideo. No website, social media or recent press coverage were found that would allow its history or current production to be reconstructed.
bruzzone-y-sciutto.flagship_grapes: Grenache; the house also sells a Marsala-style wine.

caluva.history: The CALUVA cooperative was formed in December 1967 by grape growers from the Colonia del Sacramento area, mostly immigrants or their children, who decided to make their own wine. In 1968 they made their first wine and began building the current winery in El Caño; from 1986 onward they converted their vineyards with vines imported from France.
highlights: Cooperative founded in December 1967; first vinification in 1968 with 40,000 kg of grapes.
Conversion to vinifera varieties imported from France from 1986 onward, completed by all members.
The El Caño locality used to be called 'Real de Vera', a name the cooperative uses for its VCP wine.
caluva.flagship_grapes: V.C.P. (Vino de Calidad Preferente, Uruguay's quality-wine category) made from vines imported from France; varieties and aging not published. Regular range: Tannat Roble, Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

cantera-montes-de-oca.history: Family project of Fernanda Montes de Oca and Julio Cantera in Peñarol Viejo, Montevideo, where the family settled in 2002 with the Establecimiento Los Teros. In 2017 they bought a 10-hectare property next to their home and in 2018 planted two white and six red varieties for a boutique winery focused on high-end wines.
highlights: Vineyard planted in 2018 with Viognier, Albariño, Merlot, Tannat, Marselan, Petit Verdot, Arinarnoa and Barbera.
Terroir Series and Selected Vineyard ranges plus rosés, with online sales of cases assembled by the customer.
10-hectare property in Peñarol Viejo, a rural area in the north of Montevideo.
cantera-montes-de-oca.flagship_grapes: Red blend from the Peñarol Viejo and Los Cerrillos vineyards; the winery presents it as its flagship wine.

cava-de-las-animas.history: Family winery located in Nueva Carrara, in the surroundings of the Sierra de las Ánimas, in Maldonado. According to its INAVI listing, the property combines vineyard with native woodland, birdlife and a farm pond, and offers a shop and tasting tours.
highlights: Family winery in the Sierra de las Ánimas, Nueva Carrara (Maldonado).
Registered with INAVI with a shop and tasting tours.

cerros-de-oro.history: Family winery registered with INAVI in Minas de Corrales, department of Rivera. According to its profile, its vineyards grow on granitic soils of the Isla Cristalina de Rivera.
highlights: Vineyards on granitic soils of the Isla Cristalina de Rivera, according to the winery.
cerros-de-oro.flagship_grapes: Orange wine (white wine with skin contact), 2025 vintage.

cofradia-de-la-sierra.history: According to its website, the winery is a project of seven friends who came together to make wines in the Sierra de Carapé (Cerro Laureles), Maldonado, about 30 minutes from Punta del Este. It offers vineyard tours with tasting and a paired multi-course menu, and has the restaurant La Jabaluna with seasonal cuisine and house wines.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a restaurant, lodging, shop and tasting tours.
Shares its grounds with family ventures in weaving, bamboo and natural cosmetics, according to INAVI.
cofradia-de-la-sierra.flagship_grapes: Red wine from Tannat; the website does not detail aging or style.

colorado-chico.history: Family winery in El Colorado, Canelones, that works as a shared project: several producers use the same winery with their own labels (Nakkal Wines, Becasina, Viggiano and Rooster). Winemakers Nicolás Monforte and Santiago Degásperi are in charge; they work with grapes from vineyards in Montevideo, Las Piedras, Las Violetas and Rocha. It receives visitors with a tour of the vineyard and winery and a tasting.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop, tasting tours and occasional events.
Located in El Colorado, a winery area of Las Brujas, Canelones.
colorado-chico.flagship_grapes: Red blend of Merlot, Tannat and Marselan (according to Vivino).

compania-uruguaya-de-vinos-del-mar.history: Winery established in Pueblo Garzón, Maldonado, born as a project of three families, with winemaking direction by the Michelini i Mufatto family. It makes only two varieties, Albariño and Pinot Noir, and has a wine bar next to the winery where it offers guided visits and tastings.
highlights: Makes only Albariño and Pinot Noir, according to El Cronista (2024).
Winemaking direction by Michelini i Mufatto, a family of Argentine winemakers from Gualtallary.
Registered with INAVI with a restaurant, a shop and tasting tours.
compania-uruguaya-de-vinos-del-mar.flagship_grapes: Albariño from Garzón (Maldonado); the top cuvée of its Albariño range, tasted by Decanter in 2021 and 2022.

consentino-hnos-sa.history: Establishment of the Cosentino family in Sauce (Canelones). Historical advertisements in the local press present it as a producer of wines and of a champagne-style cider.
highlights: Registered with INAVI in the Cider House category (Canelones)

damian-blengio.history: Family winery in Sauce (Canelones) that sells under the brand Vinos Al Toque. The Blengio family is linked to the origins of Bodega Mederos.

de-lucca-wines.history: The De Lucca and Galerato families arrived from Italy in the early 20th century and, before World War II, began growing vines in El Colorado, Canelones. Commercial wine sales began in 1945. Today it is run by agronomist Reinaldo De Lucca and his children, the third and fourth generations.
highlights: LSQA sustainability certification (INAVI Sustainable Viticulture Program) since 2022.
Vertisol soils with high clay content and significant lime content, on the slopes of El Colorado.
According to the winery, its vineyards lie within the Humedales de Santa Lucía protected area.
de-lucca-wines.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Sauvignon 40%, Merlot 40% and Tannat 20% (2011 vintage) from Rincón del Colorado, Canelones; age-worthy red, oak aging not detailed.

domaine-de-larvol.history: French-funded venture with a vineyard in Paso Hondo, Tacuarembó, north of San Gregorio de Polanco, planted since 2011 on sandy sandstone soils that are poor and very well drained. Winemaker Fernando Pettenuzzo chose the plots and makes the wines; the grapes are transported about 350 km to Finca Giacobbe, in Montevideo, where they are vinified. The first commercial vintage was the Areniscas Chardonnay 2020.
highlights: One of the few vineyards in Tacuarembó, in Paso Hondo
Sandstone soils, hence the name of the Areniscas line
Vinified at Finca Giacobbe (Montevideo), 350 km from the vineyard
domaine-de-larvol.flagship_grapes: Red blend from its own vineyard in Tacuarembó; the shop does not specify the grapes (the vineyard's red varieties are Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec and Pinot Noir).

dominio-cassis.history: Producer led by Carlos Tomasi, who in 1999, together with winemaker Juan Ferreri, bought a 20-hectare property near Lomas de La Paloma with 11 hectares of vines. Its fine wines come from there; its table wines come from vineyards in rural Montevideo.
highlights: 11-hectare vineyard in Rocha, near Lomas de La Paloma, on Ruta 15.
Coastal-style labels such as Oceánico Albariño, Bruma Marina and Viñedos de la Costa Tannat.
dominio-cassis.flagship_grapes: The winery's top-of-the-range red; blend and aging not published.

don-pedro.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the name Don Pedro, in the name of Gustavo Castellucio Morales, on Ruta 67 in Sauce, Canelones. The contact email suggests it operates alongside a farm under the name Los Dos Hermanos. No website or press coverage was found.

ebidol.history: INAVI registration in the name of the company Ebidol S.A., with an address on Ruta 9 around km 130, in Maldonado. The registered contact is an accounting firm, not the winery. No wine brand, website or press coverage associated with this company name was found.

el-capricho.history: Small family winery in Villa del Carmen, Durazno, founded in 2010 on a 200-hectare estate bought by Dirk Reinicke, a German based in Argentina, and a partner. It has 7 hectares of vineyard in 17 plots planted in 2003 and 2004, and winemaker Javier Alegresa produces the Art Collection, Reserve and Aguará Special Reserve ranges.
highlights: Clay vertisol soils with calcareous veins in the bedrock, according to the winery.
Grapes certified under a sustainability program since 2023, according to the official website.
Aguará Tannat Blend: 93 points from Descorchados and 90 from Tim Atkin, according to SWG.
el-capricho.flagship_grapes: Tannat and Tannat Blend, 18 months in new French oak barrels; only in the best vintages

bodega-el-legado.history: Luis Marzuca, a merchant and wine lover, planted his first vines in 1968. After his death, the family sold part of the land and leased the rest. In 2007 his son Bernardo Marzuca bought the land back and set up an artisanal boutique winery in Colonia Estrella, which also operates as an inn.
highlights: It produces about 9,000 bottles a year (El Observador, 2020).
Vineyard trained on a free vertical cordon, which gives more sun exposure and early ripening.
A four-room inn among the vineyards and a tour with tasting, picada platter and asado.

escuela-de-vitivinicultura.history: Public agricultural school of UTU (Uruguay's public technical education system), operating since 1939 on a 23-hectare property in El Colorado; its main building, from 1944, is a National Historic Monument. It is the only institution in the country that trains viticulture and winemaking technologists and has graduated some 750 winemakers. It produces about 30,000 liters a year under the 1944 label, which are not sold to the public.
highlights: The only school in Uruguay that awards the Tecnólogo en Vitivinicultura degree, with a curriculum based on the OIV.
Main building from 1944 declared a National Historic Monument.
Winery among the first 16 certified for sustainability in 2022; in 2023 it opened a distillation room and bottling line.

establecimiento-juanico.history: The property belonged to the Jesuits in the 18th century and in 1830 passed to Francisco Juanicó, an immigrant from Mahón, when vineyards were already on record. In the mid-20th century it passed to the State (Ancap). In 1979 it was bought by banker Juan Carlos Deicas; today it is run by Fernando Deicas, with his son Santiago as winemaker.
highlights: It was the first winery to plant in Garzón (Maldonado), in 2006, with 17 ha, according to Jamie Goode.
'Suelo Invertido' plot: soil layers inverted to leave calcareous clay at the surface.
Between 1945 and 1946, Ancap planted vines donated by France there to produce Juanicó cognac.
establecimiento-juanico.flagship_grapes: Red blend that varies by vintage (2015 Lote 102: Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot and Marselan); there is also a white Preludio

establecimiento-valle-maria-ltda.history: Wine estate registered with INAVI on Ruta 82, in the Pando area of Canelones. The official listing shows it with a shop and tasting tours, but publishes no history or wines.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a shop and tasting tours in Pando, Canelones.
establecimiento-valle-maria-ltda.flagship_grapes: Tannat and Merlot blend; also a Cabernet Sauvignon in 3 L packaging.

establecimientos-vicca.history: Wine cooperative of 23 family producers from Canelones, based in Las Piedras. According to the cooperative, its strength lies in bringing producers together to make and market wine jointly. It sells under the Narradores, Razapura and Notas brands and a range of frizzante wines.
highlights: Cooperative of 23 family producers from Canelones.
Narradores, Razapura and Notas brands, plus white and rosé Moscato frizzante.
Listed in the Uruguay XXI exporters' catalogue.
establecimientos-vicca.flagship_grapes: Tannat, presented on the website as 'our emblematic grape'; no aging details

familia-dardanelli.history: Founded in 1949 by Constante Dardanelli in rural Montevideo. His eldest son, Dino Dardanelli, together with his brothers, led a new stage of winemaking, and today the second, third and fourth generations work side by side in the company, with Gabriel Sánchez and Alba Dardanelli at the helm. It opened to wine tourism in 2018.
highlights: 100% family-owned winery founded in 1949; four generations work in it.
Certified in Sustainable Viticulture since 2022, among the first six wineries in the country according to the winery.
Entusiastas range: natural wines with no added sulfites, according to the official website.
familia-dardanelli.flagship_grapes: Tannat and Marselan; red with no added sulfites from the Entusiastas range, made in open barrels (botte aperto).

familia-traversa.history: Carlos Domingo Traversa arrived in Uruguay in 1904, the son of Italian immigrants, and as a young man worked as a vineyard laborer. In 1937 he and his wife, María Josefa Salort, bought 5 hectares in Montevideo, and in 1956 he founded the winery with his sons Dante, Luis and Armando.
highlights: Capacity of 11 million liters; the winery presents itself as Uruguay's largest producer.
More than 300 ha of its own in Cuchilla Pereira (Montevideo) and Paso Cuello (Canelones).
Paso Cuello: calcareous silty-clay soils on hills; Cuchilla Pereira is 15 km from the sea.
familia-traversa.flagship_grapes: Marselan, Tannat and Merlot from Paso Cuello (Canelones); six months in American oak barrels; 13.5% abv.

favretto-dragone.history: Family winery in Costa de Pando that has made wine since 1936; its name joins the surnames of the founding families, Favretto and Dragone. Today it is run by a new generation, made up of women according to INAVI, which relaunched the Favretto varietal range in 2024. It has a capacity of 450,000 liters and vineyards undergoing conversion.
highlights: Has made wine since 1936 in Costa de Pando; winery capacity of 450,000 liters.
Nutrient-rich silty clay soils, as the winery describes them; vineyards in a conversion phase.
Grows Tannat, Merlot, Malbec, Arinarnoa, Cabernet Sauvignon, Viognier, Ugni Blanc and Muscat of Alexandria.
favretto-dragone.flagship_grapes: Tannat; the winery also makes a co-fermented Tannat-Viognier and a barrel-aged Tannat

finca-buena-vista.history: Old table-wine winery in Punta Gorda, near Carmelo, whose building dates from 1940. The Bonomi family bought it and converted it to make fine wines, with winemaker Caterina Viña in charge. It produces about 15,000 bottles a year and visits are arranged through the Casa Chic hotel.
highlights: 1940 building, a former table-wine winery converted to fine wines by the Bonomi family.
Produces about 15,000 bottles a year (El Observador, 2019).
Part of the seven-winery Carmelo route created in 2017.
finca-buena-vista.flagship_grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; El Observador (2019) presents the 2017 vintage as its flagship wine

finca-consentido.history: A young family vineyard in the hills of Rocha, near Velázquez, which presents itself as the easternmost vineyard in Uruguay. Its first harvests, 2020 and 2021, were released under the El Inmaduro line, with Tannat, Merlot and Marselan.
highlights: It presents itself as the easternmost vineyard in Uruguay (a claim made by the estate).
Vineyard on hillside slopes in Rocha, with Tannat, Merlot, Marselan and Chardonnay.
El Inmaduro, Rompecorazones (Tannat 2021) and Incondicional (Chardonnay 2023) lines.
finca-consentido.flagship_grapes: Tannat, Merlot and Marselan; hand-harvested, fermented for 7 to 10 days and bottle-aged for at least three months, with no barrel aging.

finca-gimenez.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the legal name Herum SRL, in the Colón neighborhood, in northwest Montevideo. No website, social media or press was found that would allow its history or production to be reconstructed.

finca-las-violetas.history: Family winery in Las Violetas, Canelones, which sets out to make world-class wines with respect for nature. Its catalogue includes an Ícono range of Tannat, red and white blends, and varietals such as Albariño, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot; it offers a shop and tasting tours.
highlights: White blend of Chardonnay, Sauvignon Gris and Albariño, and a red of Cabernet Franc, Syrah and Marselan.
The winery describes clay to sandy soils of medium fertility and rainfall of up to 1,100 mm in Canelones.
Registered with INAVI with a shop and tasting tours.

finca-piedra.history: 600-hectare estate in Mal Abrigo, San José, next to the Sierras de Mahoma, combining a hotel, a restaurant and a winery with 20 hectares of vineyard. It presents itself as a family project of French origin, with winery equipment imported from France and Portugal. It operates under the company name Mal Abrigo S.A. Agropecuaria.
highlights: 20 hectares of vineyard within a 600-hectare estate, according to INAVI and the official website.
Ecotourism complex with a hotel, the 'El Tannat' restaurant and tours on horseback or by bicycle.
Located about 125 km from Montevideo and 110 km from Colonia, next to the Sierras de Mahoma.
finca-piedra.flagship_grapes: Merlot; reserva red with time in oak, 13.5% abv.

finca-riviera.history: Estate in Dolores (Soriano), on the banks of the Uruguay River, that makes a blend of Tannat and Cabernet Franc.
highlights: One of the few wineries registered in Soriano, in the western littoral of the country.
finca-riviera.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat and Cabernet Franc from a vineyard on the banks of the Uruguay River, in Dolores (Soriano).

fourment.history: Family winery in Canelón Chico, Canelones, registered with INAVI as Fourment Hnos. Ltda., on Ruta 32 km 29. It markets at least a Tannat Roble and a Merlot under the Bodega Fourment brand.
highlights: Winery in the Canelón Chico area, one of the traditional wine-growing hubs of Canelones.

francisco-gallo.history: Bodega Casa de Gallo, owned by Francisco Gallo and Bibiana Menza, in Canelones. It took part in wine events of the Rotary Club of Canelones.

bodega-gimenez-mendez.history: Luis Alberto Giménez ran the family wine business from 1965. In 1991, with his wife Marta Méndez, he bought a winery in the city of Canelones to make fine wines. In 2000 he made his first export, to the United States. Today his youngest son, Mauro Giménez Méndez, heads winemaking.
highlights: Its 100 Años Tannat won a Grand Mention Diploma at Vinitaly 1998, its first international award.
In 2006 it launched Uruguay's first Arinarnoa, according to the winery.
Marta Méndez founded the Asociación de Bodegas Exportadoras del Uruguay.
bodega-gimenez-mendez.flagship_grapes: Tannat; micro-vinification from the Búho series, co-fermented reds; 94 points from Tim Atkin in 2015.

goyetche.history: Winery in Sauce, Canelones, registered with INAVI as Goyetche Sauce SRL (its email reads 'Bodega y Viñedos Goyetche'). Six labels appear on Vivino: a barrel Tannat, a Gewürztraminer, a Cabernet Sauvignon, two Malbec and Syrah blends (one with Marselan) and a demi-sec sparkling wine. No website or press coverage of its history was found.
highlights: Its range includes Malbec and Syrah blends, an unusual combination among the small wineries of Canelones.

gregorio-lugano-sa.history: Winery registered with INAVI under the company name Gregorio Lugano S.A., on Avenida José Belloni in Peñarol Viejo, in the rural area of northern Montevideo. No website, social media or press coverage was found that would allow its history or current production to be reconstructed.

vinos-finos-h-stagnari.history: Héctor Stagnari and his wife Virginia Moreira completed the construction of the winery in La Puebla (La Paz, Canelones) in 2000, next to the family residence dating from 1890. They work with their own grapes: whites from La Puebla and reds from La Caballada, in Salto, where Pascual Harriague grew Tannat in the 19th century.
highlights: Red-grape vineyard in La Caballada (Salto), the area where Harriague grew Tannat in the 19th century.
La Caballada soils: sandy clay at the surface and rounded cobbles at depth, according to the winery.
600,000-liter winery with an underground cellar, completed in 2000 in La Puebla.

hacienda-del-sacramento.history: First-generation boutique winery located on Ruta 50, a few kilometers from Colonia del Sacramento. It presents itself as a producer of fine wines focused on varietal expression, with Tannat, Merlot, Pinot Noir and Viognier, and claims international awards without detailing them.
highlights: First-generation boutique winery a few kilometers from Colonia del Sacramento.
Loam-textured soils with high organic matter, analyzed every year according to the winery.
Makes Tannat, Merlot, Pinot Noir (red and rosé) and Viognier.
hacienda-del-sacramento.flagship_grapes: Two-variety blend of Tannat and Merlot; the website highlights it as an 'award-winning' and multi-award-winning wine, with no aging details

hector-peluffo.history: Family winery founded in 1970 on Camino Paso del Medio, near Ruta 67 (Canelones). It makes wine from its own grapes and in 2024 won its first gold medal.
hector-peluffo.flagship_grapes: Tannat, 2023 vintage; the winery is beginning to make preferred-quality wine (VCP).

juan-toscanini-e-hijos-sa.history: Juan Toscanini and his wife María Bianchi arrived from Genoa in 1894 and settled in Canelón Chico as farm laborers. In 1908 Juan founded his own winery, with a first production of 4,200 liters sold under the La Fuente brand. Today the family company farms some 90 hectares in Canelón Chico and Paso Cuello.
highlights: Winery founded in 1908 by Genoese immigrants; still in the hands of the Toscanini family.
90 hectares of vineyard in Canelón Chico and Paso Cuello, hand-harvested.
Offers scheduled visits to the winery and vineyards with tasting.
juan-toscanini-e-hijos-sa.flagship_grapes: 100% Tannat, 18 months in French oak barrels, bottled unfiltered; limited edition of 1,908 bottles

la-bodeguita-del-cacho.history: La Bodeguita del Cacho is in Puntas de Canelón Chico (Canelones) and is the winery of Cacho Piccardo and Olga Silva, whose Italian grandfather planted vines on the same property. Cacho made wine from 1974 with a partner, replanted the vineyard in the 1990s (from Isabella, locally 'uva frutilla', to Muscat, Tannat and Cabernet Sauvignon) and since 1999 has made wine in his own small winery, selling it in bulk. In 2019 he was joined by Spanish oenologist Olga Pascual, who holds a doctorate in oenology and is the partner of his son Diego Piccardo; she leads the shift towards fine wines under the winery's own label, launched in October 2020.
highlights: Spanish winemaker Olga Pascual, PhD in Oenology
9983 KM wine: the distance between the home towns of the couple who founded the project
Also makes a Solera and a Spanish-style vermouth
la-bodeguita-del-cacho.flagship_grapes: Oak-aged Tannat; the winery's first fine wine, 2020 vintage, made by Spanish winemaker Olga Pascual.

la-geovana-ltda.history: La Geovana Ltda. is the company name of Bodega Rovere, a family winery in Paraje Bañado (Camino a José Ignacio), in the department of San José. According to the Bodegas de Uruguay directory, it was founded by Italian immigrants, is now run by the fourth generation and has a capacity of about 370,000 liters. It receives visitors with vineyard and winery tours, tastings, platters and participatory harvests, and sells wines, jams and cheeses on site.
highlights: Operates as Bodega Rovere
Fourth-generation family winery of Italian origin
Ice wine '160 Aniversario Ice Cabernet Sauvignon' listed on Vivino
la-geovana-ltda.flagship_grapes: Varietal red Arinarnoa; the source gives no further details on style.

la-mariposa-sa.history: La Mariposa SA appears in the INAVI winery registry with a facility at Ruta 69 km 27.500, Canelones. The listing includes no email, website, commercial brand or coordinates, and no online presence of its own was found.

los-cerros-de-san-juan.history: The German Lahusen family, engaged in shipping and the wool trade, established the estate in 1854, first as a sheep farm; the vineyard and winery came decades later. It was declared a Historic Monument in 2004 and in 2019 was bought by Argentine investors.
highlights: Declared a Historic Monument in 2004; the press describes it as Uruguay's oldest active winery.
It preserves a 'museum vineyard' replanted in 1891 after phylloxera, with vines about 130 years old.
Stony terrain by the San Juan River, with a wide temperature range between day and night.
los-cerros-de-san-juan.flagship_grapes: Red blend of estate varieties (not published) with grapes from the Viña Museo, more than 120 years old; four barrels chosen from about fifty; more than two years in new French oak; 13.2% abv.

los-nadies-bodega-almacen.history: Project of the fourth generation of a family that has made wine in Uruguay since 1923 and which, according to its website, has spent more than 90 years on the same terroir. It sells directly to consumers from its winery-store and offers vineyard tours and pairing dinners. It grows Tannat, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc and Sauvignon Gris.
highlights: Fourth generation of a wine family active in Uruguay since 1923, according to the winery.
Deep clay loam and calcareous soils on gentle slopes, according to the winery's own description.
Winery-store model with direct sales, guided visits and pairing dinners with chefs.
los-nadies-bodega-almacen.flagship_grapes: Tannat and Merlot; age-worthy red, the 2021 with 18 months in new French and American oak.

luz-culinary-wine-lodge.history: A gastronomic lodge opened in 2021 on a 15-hectare property near José Ignacio, with 4 hectares of vines and one of olive trees. It has no winery of its own: its first harvest, in 2021, was vinified at Bodega Garzón, and its wines are now made by Compañía Uruguaya de Vinos.
highlights: Estate vineyard of Tannat, Merlot and Tempranillo; the wines are made at Compañía Uruguaya de Vinos.
It receives winemaking advice from the Michelini Muffato family, according to its own website.
The first harvest, in 2021, was vinified at Bodega Garzón.
luz-culinary-wine-lodge.flagship_grapes: Tannat 85% and Tempranillo 15%, co-fermented in a concrete tank; red with 20 months in French oak barrels (2022 vintage).

marichal-wines.history: Isabelino Marichal and Juana Lugano planted the family's first vineyards in Etchevarría, Canelones, including Tannat. In 1938, Juana and her children created a small winery with underground cement vats. Today it is run by the fourth generation, winemakers Alejandro and Juan Andrés Marichal, who work only with their own grapes.
highlights: Tannat Marichal 2018: No. 61 in Wine Spectator's Top 100 of 2020, the only Uruguayan wine on the list.
Clay-loam and calcareous soils on gentle rolling hills, 25 km from the Río de la Plata.
Fourth generation: winemakers Alejandro and Juan Andrés Marichal run the vineyard and winery.

marsiler-sa.history: Marsiler SA appears in the INAVI winery registry with a facility at Ruta 5 km 38.500, Canelones, in the Juanicó area. The listing includes no commercial brand or website, and no online presence of its own was found.

mataojo.history: Bodega Mataojo is located in Solís de Mataojo (Lavalleja), near the Aguas Blancas dam on the Mataojo stream. The Philipson family bought the La Poderosa farm in 2004 looking for a place for a stud farm and, inspired by Portuguese friends who make wine, founded the winery there. It produces about 60,000 bottles per year from Tannat, Merlot, Touriga Nacional, Albariño, Marselan and Cabernet Sauvignon, and exports to Brazil.
highlights: One of the few Uruguayan wineries with Touriga Nacional (red and rosé)
Albariño Nature, traditional method (champenoise)
About 60,000 bottles per year
mataojo.flagship_grapes: Red blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Tannat, Touriga Nacional and Marselan, according to Vivino.

bodega-montes-toscanini.history: Montes Toscanini emerged in 1979, when Margot Toscanini de Montes and her brother bought a winery in Las Piedras, as an offshoot of the Toscanini family, which had made its first wine in Canelones in 1908. Since 1995 it has focused on fine wines, under the direction of winemaker Leonardo Montes Toscanini.
highlights: Grand Gold Medal in official Uruguayan competitions in 14 years between 2001 and 2022, according to the winery.
Toscanini family roots: first wine made in Canelones in 1908.
Making fine wines since 1995; led by winemaker Leonardo Montes Toscanini, the fourth generation.
bodega-montes-toscanini.flagship_grapes: Tannat from selected plots with a maximum yield of 6,000 kg/ha; maceration of more than 22 days, malolactic fermentation, time in concrete and 18 months in oak barrels (type not stated), plus bottle aging.

narbona.history: The estancia's main house dates from 1909 and, according to South America Wine Guide, one of the country's first wineries operated there. The property became a tourism venture in 1990, the current vineyards were planted from 1998 onward, and construction of a new winery began in 2010.
highlights: Its boutique hotel is part of the Relais & Châteaux network, according to La Nación (2026).
Carmelo vineyard soils with about 80% limestone, according to South America Wine Guide.
Winemaker Valeria Chiola, in charge since the start of the winery's modern production.
Winery registered with INAVI in Progreso, on Ruta 5 km 31.200, a historic wine-growing area of Canelones.

penitente-arya.history: Arya is a brand of Deep Licores, a beverage company based in the Parque Agroalimentario Canario in Las Piedras (Canelones), which also produces the Deep, The Black, Paso del Calpino and Vaca Loca Cocktails brands. Under Arya it sells fruit wines (Fruit Wine), the Arya Épico line and Bianco and Rosso vermouth, and sells online through antojos.uy.
highlights: Arya brand: flavored wines (white with passion fruit, rosé with red berries, Chardonnay with blue curaçao and with pear) according to Vivino
penitente-arya.flagship_grapes: Flavored wine: a Sauvignon Blanc base with passion fruit.

piccardo-familia-de-vinos.history: Family winery in Canelones registered with INAVI on Ruta 67 km 27,5, with Néstor Piccardo as contact. It markets wines under the Piccardo brand, among them a single-plot Tannat Reserva and a red blend of Tannat, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon.
highlights: Makes a single-plot Tannat Reserva ('Parcela Uno') and a Tannat-Merlot-Cabernet Sauvignon Red Blend.
piccardo-familia-de-vinos.flagship_grapes: Tannat; deep violet red with notes of ripe fruit, spice and vanilla, tannic structure and a long finish

piccolo-banfi.history: Wine project in Cufré, Colonia, in a rolling area near the Río de la Plata, under the technical supervision of winemaker Caterina Viña. According to INAVI, its first wine was a blend of Tannat and Petit Verdot, and it also makes small lots of Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Tannat and Merlot.
highlights: Vineyard in Cufré, Colonia, on gentle slopes near the Río de la Plata.
Technical supervision by winemaker Caterina Viña, also in charge of Buena Vista in Carmelo.
Exclusive lots of Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Tannat and Merlot, according to INAVI.
piccolo-banfi.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat and Petit Verdot, presented by INAVI as the project's first wine, with regional character

pisano-artesania-en-vinos-finos.history: Francesco Pisano arrived in Uruguay in 1870. His son Césare Secundino Pisano settled in Progreso in 1914, planted the original vineyards and made his first wine from the 1924 harvest. Today the winery is run by his grandsons Daniel, Eduardo and Gustavo Pisano.
highlights: Cisplatino Tannat 2015 (for Marks & Spencer): Platinum Best in Show, Decanter World Wine Awards 2017.
Exporting since 1998; the United Kingdom was its first market.
It uses integrated, organic or biodynamic management depending on plot and vintage, according to South America Wine Guide.
pisano-artesania-en-vinos-finos.flagship_grapes: Tannat; Gran Reserva made only in the best vintages, with a minimum of 18 months in new French oak barrels and 12 months in bottle before release.

pizzorno-family-estates.history: The Pizzorno family has been making wine in Canelón Chico since 1910, across four generations. In 1988 winemaker Carlos Pizzorno, now the director, steered the winery toward fine wines, which opened the way to its first exports. His wife, Ana Laura Rodríguez, and his children Francisco and María Clara are also involved.
highlights: 21 ha around the winery, on shallow clay-loam, calcareous soils over gentle rolling hills.
It works only with its own grapes from 12 varieties, with hand harvesting and no soil fertilization.
It offers guided tours, a restaurant and an inn at the winery itself.
pizzorno-family-estates.flagship_grapes: Blend of Tannat 48%, Cabernet Franc 23%, Marselan 20% and Petit Verdot 9% (2023), Canelones vineyards; 12 months in new French Allier oak and another 12 after blending.

pueblo-tannat.history: Pueblo Tannat is a family winery and restaurant venture in Colonia Estrella, Carmelo (Colonia), listed with INAVI under the legal name Bañados Naturales SA. The grapes come from the Pueblo Tannat estate, located near the winery. The establishment is open every day, offers visits and tastings, and the restaurant serves grilled meats and pasta.
highlights: Registered with INAVI with a restaurant, shop and tasting tours in Carmelo.
pueblo-tannat.flagship_grapes: Red blend (the winery does not specify the grapes), of very limited production and one year in French and American oak barrels.

bodega-sacromonte.history: A project of Peruvian Edmond Borit, grandson of a French winemaker who founded wineries in Peru, on a property of more than 100 hectares in the Sierra de Carapé. The vineyard was established between 2014 and 2017 and has produced wines since 2018; the property also operates as a hotel.
highlights: Gold medal at the Decanter World Wine Awards 2022 for its Tannat 2020.
Vineyard on the northern slope of the Sierra de Carapé, on a largely undisturbed property.
It makes six red varieties, including Tannat, Marselan and Cabernet Franc.
bodega-sacromonte.flagship_grapes: Co-fermentation of Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Syrah and Marselan

highlights: According to INAVI, it makes wines for bulk sale, with no bottled brand of its own.

santa-elena.flagship_grapes: Red table wine from Montevideo, 10% alcohol, in a 1 L bottle; also a sweet red and a rosé.

santiago-giacobbe-sa.history: The Giacobbe family descends from Genoese immigrants who settled on the outskirts of Montevideo in the mid-19th century. Around 1903 the founders, Juan Pedro Domingo and Antonio Giacobbe, settled in Manga, where they grew mainly Harriague vines (now Tannat) and later began to make and sell wine.
highlights: Family of Genoese origin settled in Manga around 1903, according to the INAVI listing.
Its first vines were Harriague, the historic name for Tannat in Uruguay.
